stories.title: Offerings at the Tabernacle
stories.summary: The LORD speaks from the tent of meeting and sets out the burnt, grain, peace, sin and guilt offerings, with rules for the priests' portions. Together they describe how Israelites approach God with sacrifice.

stories.title: Aaron and His Sons Are Ordained
stories.summary: Moses washes, clothes and anoints Aaron and his sons over seven days. On the eighth day they offer the first sacrifices and fire from the LORD consumes the offering on the altar.

stories.title: Nadab and Abihu
stories.summary: Aaron's sons Nadab and Abihu offer unauthorized fire and are consumed by fire from the LORD. Moses forbids mourning by Aaron and his remaining sons and gives instructions about wine and the priests' portions.

stories.title: Clean and Unclean Animals
stories.summary: God distinguishes land animals, sea creatures, birds and insects that may be eaten from those that may not, and tells Israel to be holy as he is holy.

stories.title: Purity After Childbirth, Skin Disease and Mold
stories.summary: Instructions cover purification after childbirth, diagnosing and cleansing skin disease, mold in houses and garments, and bodily discharges.

stories.title: The Day of Atonement
stories.summary: Once a year the high priest enters the most holy place with blood and incense to atone for himself, the priests and the people. A goat is sent into the wilderness bearing Israel's sins.

stories.title: Holiness Laws
stories.summary: God sets rules on blood, forbidden sexual relations, neighborly conduct, penalties for serious offenses, and priestly purity. The refrain is 'be holy, for I the LORD your God am holy'.

stories.title: The Appointed Festivals
stories.summary: The Sabbath, Passover, Unleavened Bread, firstfruits, Pentecost, trumpets, Day of Atonement and Tabernacles are set as fixed feasts of the LORD.

stories.title: The Blasphemer Stoned
stories.summary: The son of an Israelite woman and an Egyptian man curses the Name in a fight. After the LORD is consulted, the congregation stones him, and the principle of equal justice for native and sojourner is restated.

stories.title: The Sabbath Year and Jubilee
stories.summary: The land rests every seventh year, and every fiftieth year property returns to its family and slaves go free. The chapter also sets rules for redeeming land and relatives.

stories.title: Blessings and Curses
stories.summary: God promises rain, peace and his presence for obedience, and escalating punishments, scattering and later remembrance of the covenant for disobedience. The book closes with rules for vows and tithes.
